Re: LD 1418 - An Act to Protect Access to Reproductive Health Care, Including Fertility Treatments and Contraceptives
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services, thank you for the opportunity to provide information in support of LD 1418, An Act to Protect Access to Reproductive Health Care, Including Fertility Treatments and Contraceptives.
This bill prohibits the Commissioner of the Department of Health and Human Services (the "Department") from adopting rules that place a ban or restriction on access to reproductive health care. The Department supports retaining broad access to reproductive health services as a matter of public health and individual rights and appreciates the intent of this bill to ensure continued access to medically necessary care and treatment for the people of Maine.
The Department strongly supports Maine's current law and public policy, as reflected in Governor Janet Mill's Executive Order 4 FY 21/22: An Order Protecting Access to Reproductive Health Care Services in Maine, to protect an individual's choices in reproductive health care. Currently, Maine ensures health coverage for reproductive health care by requiring public and private health insurers to cover family planning services, abortion services, and pregnancy-related services in accordance with applicable law.
Practically speaking, this bill codifies the existing coverage of reproductive health care services to MaineCare members as well as other individuals receiving reproductive health services through various Departmental programs. MaineCare currently reimburses for a wide range of reproductive health services with no cost-sharing to all members with full MaineCare coverage or Limited Family Planning Benefit. Abortions not eligible for federal funds (those that do not qualify under Hyde Act exceptions) are provided under the MaineCare program using state-only funds. Fertility treatment is not currently covered by MaineCare.
Dorothea Dix Psychiatric Center and Riverview Psychiatric Center provide general reproductive healthcare and contraceptives on a case-by-case basis; community consultations are made for complex cases requiring specialist care. While fertility treatment is not offered by these facilities, interested patients are connected via follow up referral and appointment in the community at time of discharge. In addition, Maine CDC's Maternal and Child Health Program oversees a contract with the Family Planning Association of Maine which provides access to clinical reproductive healthcare statewide.

The Department would like to note that it is possible that strict interpretation of the language as drafted could provide a disincentive for the introduction of new coverage of reproductive health care services, if a rule to provide this expanded coverage were also to include limits around the application of or eligibility for this coverage, as one could regard anything less than full coverage for all to qualify as a "restriction on access to reproductive health care...." The Department strongly supports what it believes is the intent of LD 1418 and would recommend an amendment to qualify that the prohibition be on a ban or restriction on existing access to reproductive health care.
Access to the full spectrum of reproductive health care is integral to a person's physical, mental, and economic well-being. Every person in Maine has the right to make their own personal medical decisions and to access sexual and reproductive health care when and where they need it. It is critical that everyone in Maine has access to affordable, high-quality health care, including reproductive services.
Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions during your deliberation of this bill.
Sincerely,
Michelle Probert Director Office of MaineCare Services Maine Department of Health and Human Services

Testimony of Suzanne Lafreniere, on behalf of the Roman Catholic Diocese in opposition to LD 1418
An Act to Protect Access to Reproductive Health Care, Including Fertility Treatments and Contraceptives
Senator Ingwerson, Representative Meyer, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services, my name is Suzanne Lafreniere and I represent the Roman Catholic Diocese of Portland in opposition to LD 1418. The Diocese has a population of over 279,000 Catholics* or onefifth of the total population of the state of Maine. In addition to its 141 churches organized into 48 parishes, it has nine elementary schools, one private elementary school, one diocesan high school and one private high school. It also includes one Catholic college, Saint Joseph's College of Maine in Standish. Within the diocese, there are also seven subsidized housing units, four rehabilitation and residence facilities, and two child-care centers. There are three Catholic hospitals operating independently of the diocese as well as Catholic Charities Maine, the state's largest social service agency, which operates as a separate corporation.
The Roman Catholic Diocese of Portland advocates for enacting and enforcing laws that create safe communities and promote the common good. This issue is important to Catholics because as people of faith a primary concern is the moral and ethical considerations that should be at the root of our decision making. We all are created in God's image. We all--each of us--possess a basic human dignity. The Catholic Church teaches that human life is sacred and that the dignity of the human person is the underpinning of a moral vision for society. This belief is the foundational principle of Catholic social teaching.
We urge the legislature to consider approaches that truly support women and families--by providing resources for mothers in need, education on natural family planning, and support for ethical medical care--rather than promoting measures that end innocent life or undermine the sanctity of marriage and family.
I urge you to vote ought to not to pass. Thank you for your time and consideration today.

Testimony ofSenator Tim Nangle introducing
LD 1418, "An Act to Protect Access to Reproductive Health Care, Including
Fertility Treatments and Contraceptives" Before the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services
April 17, 2025
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and distinguished colleagues of the Joint Standing Committee
on Health and Human Services, as you know, my name is Tim Nangle, and I proudly represent Senate
District 26, which includes Casco, Frye Island, Raymond, Windham, and part of Westbrook. Thank you
for the opportunity to present LD 1418, "An Act to Protect Access to Reproductive Health Care,
Including Fertility Treatments and Contraceptives."
As I began working on this bill, it became clear that the current language was not quite ready for prime
time. I am working with stakeholders and experts, and we're confident that with more time and continued collaboration, we can bring forward a stronger version that better reflects the goals we're trying to
achieve.
At the same time, I am mindful that the national legal landscape for reproductive health care is changing
quickly. With several major court decisions expected in the coming months ----- and with executive and administrative actions shifting at a rapid pace --- it makes sense to take the time to ensure that our policy response is durable and well-informed.
For those reasons, I respectfully ask the Committee to carry over LD 1418 to the next legislative session.
I believe that this would give us the appropriate time to ensure that any legislation we adopt has a
meaningful impact on protecting access to reproductive care.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,
Tim Nangle
